title: Ladybug screen print
lede: Charley Harper reduces a ladybug to a red half-disc with two black dots, set against a gray ground with stylized grass stems.
summary: A red half-disc ladybug with black dots, thin black legs, and tan grass on gray. Charley Harper, 1959.

evidence.note: Based on the Cincinnati Art Museum record. The museum serves only a 600 × 446 px image, below this catalogue’s 800 px threshold for observed evidence, so the observations below are provisional. Not stored.

styles.note: Harper reduces animals to flat geometric planes, a core trait of the illustrative side of the style.

context: The Cincinnati Art Museum catalogues Ladybug as a color screen print by Charley Harper (American, 1922–2007), dated 1959; composition 32.9 × 47 cm on a 38.7 × 52 cm sheet; Gift of the Estate of Charley Harper; accession number 2009.67. [Cincinnati Art Museum](https://collection.cincinnatiartmuseum.org/objects/26803/ladybug).
Harper’s serigraphs grew out of his bird paintings for *Ford Times* in the 1950s. [Charley Harper Art Studio](https://www.charleyharperartstudio.com/ford-times-retrospective).
observed: From the 600 px museum image: a large red shape, a half-disc with a straight edge, carries two black circles. A small black head with cream eyes sits at its straight edge.
Thin black legs and antennae are drawn as straight segments.
Tan grass stems and seed heads rise at the left beside a black vertical bar, on a flat gray ground with a few speckled dark patches.
interpretation: The insect is built from a circle cut in half and two dots: the reduction to a few flat planes that the style’s rubric names.
The saturated red is an exception to the muted palette, used as a single accent on gray.
borrow: Reduce a creature to one geometric shape plus two or three details.
Use one saturated accent on a quiet gray or cream ground.
next: Find an image of this print or another 1950s Harper serigraph at 800 px or more, and review the observations.

rights.statement: No image is stored. Charley Harper died in 2007; the work is in copyright.
